name: Ceylon cinnamon
summary: Ceylon cinnamon is the dried inner bark of Cinnamomum verum, sold as rolled sticks or powder. This page lists what people say cinnamon does and what writers in ancient Greece and Rome believed; each claim can be checked against the research when you choose.
inIt: Ceylon (true) cinnamon is the inner bark of Cinnamomum verum. Other barks sold simply as 'cinnamon' are cassia species (C. cassia, C. burmannii, C. loureiroi).

In a US analysis, C. verum bark held only traces of coumarin, while all three cassia barks held substantial amounts. Coumarin was found in every cinnamon, cinnamon-flavoured food and cinnamon supplement bought in shops there, and the samples were probably Indonesian cassia.
Coumarin can harm the liver. Europe uses a tolerable daily intake of 0.1 mg per kg of body weight per day.
In a 4-week crossover trial in 11 healthy people, about 6% of cinnamon's oxalate was water soluble (91% in turmeric), and cinnamon did not raise urinary oxalate significantly.

The UK food table (CoFID) measures ground cinnamon at 53.1 g of fibre, 1,002 mg of calcium, 431 mg of potassium and 8.3 mg of iron per 100 g, but does not say which species it is and gives no energy value. A teaspoon is only about 3 g.

lore.belief: Dioscorides called all cinnamon warming, diuretic, softening and digestive, and good against the poison of venomous animals and against deadly poisons.
lore.note: The ancient writers' 'cinnamon' and 'cassia' are named by their own words and by modern editors' suggestions; it is not certain that their bark was the Sri Lankan species sold today as Ceylon cinnamon.

lore.belief: Dioscorides wrote that cinnamon rubbed on with honey takes away freckles and sunburn, that it is good for coughs, mucous discharges, dropsy, kidney diseases and difficult urination, and that it cleans away what darkens the pupils of the eyes.

processing: Coumarin differs by species, not by form: the US analysis found it in every cinnamon supplement and cinnamon-flavoured food it tested, and judged them probably cassia.

claims.claim: Ceylon cinnamon is safer than ordinary cinnamon because it has less coumarin
claims.label: Ceylon cinnamon and coumarin

whoShouldBeCareful.with: Liver disease, or a lot of ordinary (cassia) cinnamon
whoShouldBeCareful.note: Cassia cinnamon holds substantial coumarin, which is known to be toxic to the liver, and cinnamon sold only as 'cinnamon' is often cassia. Ceylon cinnamon held only traces. If you have liver problems, talk to your doctor.
A drug-and-lactation review says no data exist on the safety of cinnamon in nursing mothers or infants. If you are breastfeeding, talk to your doctor or midwife.

unknowns: Whether eating cinnamon in food changes blood sugar or other health outcomes in people: this page does not review the trials.
How much coumarin a given jar holds: the label rarely says which species it is.
Whether Ceylon cinnamon works differently from cassia in the body beyond its coumarin.
